name: file_carver
description: Cut ONE candidate file out of a raw dump at a known offset: from the offset to the end the format's own structure gives, with its SHA-256, optionally written to a new file (an existing file is never replaced). A candidate fragment, not a recovered file: the result says boundary: validated when a structure walk reached the format's end (PNG chunk CRCs to IEND, JPEG markers to EOI, GIF blocks to the trailer, a ZIP end record whose offsets agree, a registry hive's hive-bin chain adding up to the size its base block states, a SQLite header with a valid page count, a PDF's last startxref pointing at an xref) and boundary: heuristic when it rests on a header field or marker that was not cross-checked (a PE's section table and certificate table, with overlay_uncertain when bytes follow). It does not show the bytes are the whole original, unfragmented or unaltered. Reads the file at path as given: a container such as an E01 is not decoded. Streams; never holds the source whole.

path.description: Path to the raw binary dump to carve from (a container such as E01 is read as its container bytes)

offset.description: Byte offset in that file where the signature starts

sig_type.description: Which format's boundary check to use: PE, ZIP, PDF, SQLite, regf, PNG, JPEG, GIF

max_size.description: Ceiling for the candidate (default 100 MB); a larger one is refused with its required size, never cut

output.description: Optional new output file under the run directory; refused if it exists. In a job it must lie under $OUT: give {OUT}/<name>, or work/extracted/<your id>/<name>, which the harness maps there. If omitted, returns metadata only.
